MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L12·N443unmasked layer
This neuron fires weakly and diffusely at clause-closing positions — chiefly the comma (or the last word completing a set phrase, e.g. "lives up to the name", "Done well") right before a qualifying/contrastive continuation like "regardless of…", "but they do not believe it"; it is a mid-sentence boundary detector rather than a semantic one (and is strongly suppressed by very similar commas/clause-final verbs such as "worked", "point,", "be").

Rather than a clean semantic feature, this unit fires on the token that *continues* a phrase immediately after a modifier/intensifier or colon — e.g. the "in" after "especially", the "self" in "much-needed self-criticism", "unit" in "dimensionless unit hydrographs", the clause-initial "It"/"there" — and is suppressed on tokens that *close* such a construction (head nouns like "-ography", "value", "users" and clause-final commas).

L12·N12683unmasked layer
This low-amplitude neuron gives its highest values on ordinary content words completing a phrase in flowing prose (e.g. "mnemonics", "outside noise", "any changes", "other cleaning"), while it is strongly *suppressed* by list-introducing punctuation and enumeration markers (comma/colon before an item list, "First,"/"Second,"), so it mainly separates continuous-prose continuation tokens from list-delimiter positions.
